title: Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act of 2025

claims.claim: Under current law, Alaska Native Village Corporations had to convey some of their land in trust to the State of Alaska to support future municipal governments.
claims.sourceSpan: conveyed to the State in trust all or a portion of the acreage of land required to be conveyed under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future
claims.note: "required to be conveyed ... to the State in trust ... for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future" backs the pre-existing conveyance obligation; "some" = "all or a portion of the acreage".

claims.claim: This bill ends that requirement going forward.
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future
claims.note: Polarity check: source removes the obligation ("shall not be required") going forward from enactment - direction matches "ends that requirement".

claims.claim: and lets a Village Corporation reclaim land it already put in trust if no municipal government was ever established.
claims.sourceSpan: on formal resolution by the Village Corporation and the residents of the Native village requesting dissolution of the trust, the trust shall be dissolved and title to the land shall revert to the Village Corporation
claims.note: Source condition is "has not been established as of that date of enactment"; "was ever established" is a faithful temporal gloss, not a change of meaning.

claims.claim: Ends the requirement that Alaska Native Village Corporations convey land in trust for future municipalities
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future

claims.claim: and allows reversion of unused trust land.
claims.sourceSpan: the trust shall be dissolved and title to the land shall revert to the Village Corporation
claims.note: "unused" glosses "a Municipal Corporation has not been established" - reasonable characterization, not stated as such in source.

claims.claim: No Future Trust Conveyance Required
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future

claims.claim: Village Corporations no longer required to convey land in trust for future municipal corporations
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future

claims.claim: Applies as of the date of enactment
claims.sourceSpan: as of the date of enactment
claims.note: Effective trigger "as of the date of enactment of the Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act of 2025".

claims.claim: Reversion of Unused Trust Land
claims.sourceSpan: the trust shall be dissolved and title to the land shall revert to the Village Corporation
claims.note: "Unused" glosses the not-established condition; core reversion mechanic is verbatim.

claims.claim: Trust land conveyed for a municipality that was never established can revert to the Village Corporation
claims.sourceSpan: a Municipal Corporation has not been established as of that date of enactment
claims.note: Reversion is triggered where "a Municipal Corporation has not been established"; "can revert" reflects the resolution-contingent "shall revert".

claims.claim: Requires a formal resolution by the Village Corporation and the village residents
claims.sourceSpan: on formal resolution by the Village Corporation and the residents of the Native village
claims.note: Both actors (Village Corporation + residents of the Native village) named in source.

claims.claim: Reversion is subject to existing rights, easements, and roadway access
claims.sourceSpan: any existing easements, rights-of-way necessary for public roadway access
claims.note: Also backed by "valid existing rights created by the applicable trust". Source additionally lists "rights-of-way for access of holders of valid existing rights" (not surfaced here - see omission row).

claims.claim: Names the Act the "Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act of 2025".
claims.sourceSpan: Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act of 2025

claims.claim: Short-title section - citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the
claims.note: Section 1 is a pure citation clause; no operative text.

claims.claim: Amends Section 14(c) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1613(c))
claims.sourceSpan: Section 14(c) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1613(c)) is amended
claims.note: Statutory cite verbatim.

claims.claim: so a Village Corporation is no longer required to convey additional land in trust to the State for the future establishment of a Municipal Corporation.
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future

claims.claim: Where a Village Corporation, before enactment, conveyed land in trust for a municipality that has not been established as of enactment, the trust may be dissolved and title revert to the Village Corporation on formal resolution by the corporation and the residents of the Native village.
claims.sourceSpan: if a Village Corporation, prior to the date of enactment of the Alaska Native Village Municipal Lands Restoration Act of 2025, conveyed to the State in trust all or a portion of the acreage of land required to be conveyed under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future, and a Municipal Corporation has not been established as of that date of enactment, on formal resolution by the Village Corporation and the residents of the Native village requesting dissolution of the trust, the trust shall be dissolved and title to the land shall revert to the Village Corporation
claims.note: Modal note: source is "shall be dissolved" upon resolution; analysis's "may be dissolved ... on formal resolution" reflects that filing the resolution is at the corporation/residents' discretion. Faithful, not an overgeneralization of the effect.

claims.claim: Reversion is subject to valid existing rights created by the trust and existing easements or rights-of-way for public roadway access
claims.sourceSpan: valid existing rights created by the applicable trust
claims.note: Also "any existing easements, rights-of-way necessary for public roadway access".

claims.claim: and the Village Corporation assumes the trust's obligations under any lease or use agreement on reversion.
claims.sourceSpan: the Village Corporation shall assume the obligations of the applicable trust with respect to any lease or other use agreement applicable to the land on reversion of the land to the Village Corporation pursuant to subclause (I)

claims.claim: The amendment also makes technical redesignations
claims.sourceSpan: by redesignating paragraphs (1) through (5) as subparagraphs (A) through (E)
claims.note: Redesignation/reformatting clauses (1)-(5) are technical, matching this characterization.

claims.claim: and fixes the relevant date as December 18, 1971.
claims.sourceSpan: December 18, 1971
claims.note: Amendment inserts "existed as of December 18, 1971." - date verbatim.

claims.claim: When trust land reverts to a Village Corporation, the corporation must assume the obligations of the applicable trust with respect to any lease or other use agreement on the land.
claims.sourceSpan: the Village Corporation shall assume the obligations of the applicable trust with respect to any lease or other use agreement applicable to the land on reversion of the land to the Village Corporation pursuant to subclause (I)
claims.note: "must assume" = "shall assume".

claims.claim: reversion carries forward the trust's existing lease and use-agreement obligations along with valid existing rights and roadway easements.
claims.sourceSpan: the Village Corporation shall assume the obligations of the applicable trust with respect to any lease or other use agreement
claims.note: Also backed by (III)(aa) "valid existing rights" + "easements, rights-of-way necessary for public roadway access".

claims.claim: The bill allows reversion of trust land where no municipality was established but does not address land already conveyed for municipalities that were established.
claims.sourceSpan: a Municipal Corporation has not been established as of that date of enactment
claims.note: Accurate gap: the reversion trigger is limited to municipalities not established; the text contains no provision for land where a municipality was established.

claims.claim: New process for dissolving a trust and reverting land to a Village Corporation where a municipality was never established
claims.sourceSpan: the trust shall be dissolved and title to the land shall revert to the Village Corporation

claims.claim: Amends Section 14(c) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1613(c)) to end required trust conveyances for future municipalities
claims.sourceSpan: Section 14(c) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1613(c)) is amended
claims.note: Cite verbatim; end-of-requirement backed by (iv)(II).

claims.claim: Removes the requirement that Village Corporations convey additional land in trust for the future establishment of a Municipal Corporation
claims.sourceSpan: a Village Corporation shall not be required to convey any additional land in trust under this subparagraph for the establishment of a Municipal Corporation in the future

claims.claim: Enacted as Public Law 119-23 on July 7, 2025.
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-23
claims.note: PL number verbatim; date backed by "Approved July 7, 2025."

claims.claim: Introduced by Rep. Nick Begich (R-AK)
claims.note: Sponsor name/party is structural metadata from Congress.gov (cache sponsor field), not present in the bill text; accurate, not a training-data fabrication. Bill text identifies the measure only as [H.R. 43]. Not material.

claims.claim: with no cosponsors
claims.note: Cosponsor count is structural metadata (cache cosponsors: 0), not in the bill source text. Accurate, not a fabrication. Not material.

claims.claim: the change to Alaska Native Village Corporation land-conveyance obligations drew no recorded opposition
claims.sourceSpan: considered and passed House
claims.note: Breadth-of-support characterization. Source states only "considered and passed" both chambers with no tallies. Cache votes[] show House 412-1 (1 nay) - so "no recorded opposition" slightly overstates; near-unanimous but not literally zero. Not material.

claims.claim: and cleared both chambers before being signed.
claims.sourceSpan: considered and passed Senate
claims.note: Both chambers' passage + signature backed by "considered and passed House", "considered and passed Senate", "Approved July 7, 2025."

claims.claim: Reversion requirements are framed "in accordance with subsection (g)" of ANCSA 14(c) - a cross-reference the analysis does not surface.
claims.sourceSpan: In accordance with subsection (g)
claims.note: Minor structural qualifier; does not change reader understanding of the reversion mechanic.

claims.claim: Source (III)(aa)(BB) also preserves "rights-of-way for access of holders of valid existing rights", beyond public roadway access; analysis's roadway phrasing omits this sub-clause.
claims.sourceSpan: or rights-of-way for access of holders of valid existing rights
claims.note: The general "existing rights, easements, and roadway access" phrasing captures the gist; this specific sub-clause is not itemized. Not material.
